items.author: Ben
items.title: Rivals buy firms too - buy_corporation joins the scored-utility candidate list
items.design: The symmetry half of BL-628 (whole-firm buyout), and a widening of the BL-202/BL-203 exception in its established shape: deterministic, seeded, scored-utility, a legal verb and never a planner. THE WORK: score buy_corporation in corp_ai.cpp's existing candidate list, capped at one acquisition per evaluation, its price carried in the candidate's spend under the solvency gate so a rival cannot buy itself below its reserve floor. Availability is gated on the target's ownership class, not on the acquirer's cash - the 'never on cash' ruling's shape. Record the grant in the standing rules with its date, as every prior widening is recorded. SAVING UP IS NOT PLANNING, and this item owns the distinction: Ben's Sprint 20 goal wants a corp to accumulate cash toward an acquisition, but a scorer that defers a cheap build today in order to afford a firm tomorrow is edging toward the planner the standing rules forbid. The honest route needs no new machinery - accumulation is EMERGENT when the buy candidate outscores the marginal build, since a tick with no affordable positive candidate simply banks its cash. Whether that actually happens at the authored weights is a measurement, and BL-634 (acquisition viability) is where it is taken.

items.title: charter_reach is computed at generation and silently zeroed on load
items.author: Ben
items.design: Found by the wave-2 review barrier. BL-638 added settlement_state::charter (a charter_reach), and w_settlement/r_settlement do not carry it. The omission is SYMMETRIC so the stream stays consistent and no version bump is owed - it is not a corruption bug. It is a LATENT one: the field is silently zeroed on load, which is benign only while the sole readers are generate_corporations and its harness, both of which run before any save exists. It becomes wrong the moment BL-627 (profitability ledger), BL-629 (rival acquisition) or the generation ledger reads charter off a LOADED world - and it will read as 'this world has no charter' rather than as an error. TWO HONEST ROUTES, pick one and say why: serialise it (a version bump, claimed through next_save_version.js), or RECOMPUTE it on load from the ladder it is derived from, which costs no format change and cannot drift from its source. The second is probably right, since charter_reach is a pure function of already-serialised state.

items.title: The eighth field - a return sees the whole quarter, not just the money loop
items.author: Ben
items.design: Ben's ruling, 2026-08-26, on NR-655/NR-668 - option A of the three-way fork, and the measurement that forced it: a firm earning through mercenary contracts files a trailing_net IDENTICAL to a firm that earns nothing there, so BL-628's buyout undervalues it by exactly 640 credits (k 8.0 x the 80/quarter the record cannot see). Design in FINANCE.md section The eighth field. THE WORK: add `other` to quarterly_return = the whole-tick balance delta minus the money-loop net, and MOVE THE FILING from the end of apply_budget to after the tick's last balance mover - which is the part that needs care, since apply_budget does not own the tick and the headless harnesses call it directly. Then re-point corp_trailing_net at the mean of (net + other) so the buyout prices off the whole quarter. THREE PROPERTIES TO ASSERT: the seven flows still explain `net` unchanged; net+other telescopes EXACTLY over a run (the retain property extended from one function to the whole tick); and BL-628's own harness row that currently PINS the 640-credit blindness must be re-specified to pin the closure instead - do not delete it, invert it. `other` is deliberately NOT itemised: split into named lines it becomes a second budget breakdown competing with corp_budget, and the reason there is one accounting authority is that two of them disagree. Versions the save format.

items.title: Decide what actually shapes background density - the ratio, or the per-resource cap
items.author: Ben
items.design:
Raised by BL-655's measurement and by its novelty flag. Pass 6 is documented as stopping on a 0.90 production/demand ratio, described as 'an emergent measurement rather than an injected clearing constant' and 'a stop condition, not a firm-count budget'. MEASURED: the ratio NEVER BINDS on the worlds we generate. `per_resource_firm_cap = 8` binds on every demanded resource, so the count is exactly specialists + 8 x basket breadth - which reproduced 104, 64 and 56 corps exactly across three configurations. Its own comment still says 'provisional - measure, then pin'. The doc has been corrected to describe what the code does; what is OPEN is which behaviour is wanted. THREE READINGS: (a) the cap is the real design and the ratio is dead weight - pin the cap deliberately, say density is breadth-driven, and delete the ratio; (b) the ratio is the real design and the cap is an emergency brake set too low - raise it until the ratio binds, which restores the 'calibrated, not authored' property the doc claims; (c) both, with the cap as a genuine guard against a pathological basket. Note the consequence either way: under (a) density becomes a function of how many DIFFERENT goods are wanted, so every demand channel Sprint 21 adds moves the world's size - which may be a feature.
--- RULED 2026-09-06 (Ben, on the doc-reconciliation form): READING (a), THE CAP IS THE DESIGN ---

Pin the cap deliberately, say density is breadth-driven, and retire the 0.90 ratio outright. The
alternative readings are both declined: raising the cap until the ratio binds would restore a
'calibrated, not authored' property the code never actually had, and keeping both would leave a
constant in the file that has never once bound on any world we generate.

THE CONSEQUENCE IS ACCEPTED, NOT OVERLOOKED, and it is now written into the authority doc:
background density is a function of HOW MANY DIFFERENT GOODS ARE WANTED, not of how much of them.
A basket that grows in breadth grows the corp count; a world consuming twice as much of the same
goods gets the same firms. That makes the demand basket's breadth a DENSITY KNOB, and anything
editing that basket is editing the size of the background economy.

WRITTEN INTO docs/generation/CORPORATION_GENERATION.md § Pass 6 - Background firm generation,
which also records that Pass 6 is a one-shot again: the economic settle it was described as
recurring through is retired by GENERATION_STRATEGY.md § The eight phases, and the background
economy's source is now the landscape phase 6 selects.

items.title: A firm underwater long enough exits - give interest the consequence it is supposed to have
items.author: Ben
items.design: MEASURED 2026-08-26 from Ben's own observation of the live build. Of 12 seeds, 3 clear with ZERO interest; the 9 that fail all dipped negative once and interest is then 43-60% of their whole loss, against an operating gap of only -24 to -40 cr/qtr. 1.02^80 = 4.9x over the warm start. The rate is not the defect - components.hpp's 'no insolvency consequence' is. A firm that would have died in year three trades for twenty and is handed to the player as wreckage. THE WORK: a firm underwater for N consecutive quarters EXITS - dissolved, or absorbed via BL-628's dissolve_into, which already moves holdings, pools, balance and returns and cancels the promises nobody is left to keep. N and the trigger are authored in economy.lua and MEASURED, not picked. DESIGN-OWED on three questions that are Ben's: (1) dissolve or absorb - absorption by a solvent neighbour is richer and reuses the buyout path, dissolution is simpler and leaves ground free; (2) does this run IN PLAY as well as in the pre-game, i.e. can the player's own corp fail - NR-670 already ruled a rival may not BUY the player out, and this is a different question about the player failing on their own account; (3) what happens to the ground and the workforce - a dissolved firm's tiles should probably become available rather than stay held. EXPECTED CONSEQUENCE, and the reason this is priority A: the field at seat time becomes self-selected for viability, so BL-630's shortlist floor should start being met instead of falling through to its fallback on 23 of 24 seeds.

items.title: The solvency gate tests the price, not the position after the debt transfers
items.author: Ben
items.design: MEASURED by BL-634, which found it by taking its own brief's gate literally. The acquisition price is max(0, book_value + k x trailing_net + balance) and the balance term is SIGNED, so a deeply indebted firm's negative cash cancels its book value, the sum goes below zero, and the floor hands it over FREE. On 5 of 8 seeds the cheapest buyable firm cost exactly 0 cr. The dissolution rule then transfers the debt at face value: one seed took on -13,358 cr for nothing, and 3 of 8 buyers that bought the cheapest firm were sunk by it. THE FLOOR IS NOT THE BUG - a worthless firm is worth nothing, and NR-648's reasoning stands. The bug is that the SOLVENCY GATE READS THE PRICE rather than the buyer's balance AFTER the transfer, which is the same shape as the non-finite-price bug BL-628 caught in its own code: a check applied to the wrong quantity. THE WORK: gate on the post-acquisition position, so a corp cannot be handed a liability it could never have chosen to take on. Then re-run acquisition_viability's --target cheapest sweep, where 'still earning after' should go 5/8 -> 8/8. Note the harness already measures BOTH gates and its --target flag exists for exactly this comparison.

items.title: Population lens: regional heatmap with harder scaling, not a per-tile mark
items.design:
Ben, 2026-08-28: "Population: Let's see what this looks like as a heatmap with more extreme scaling. This way we should be able to see population regionally, not just on each tile."

Today the lens draws "per-tile value marks, workforce efficiency" (LENSES.md routing table) - a per-tile read, which is why a region of moderate population and a region of none look similar at whole-planet zoom. Two changes: a continuous heatmap fill rather than discrete marks, and a scaling curve steep enough that regional differences separate instead of compressing into the middle of the ramp.

EXPLICITLY AN EXPERIMENT, in Ben's own framing - "let's see what this looks like". The deliverable is a capture to rule on, not a settled design; expect a second pass on the curve. Worth measuring the actual population distribution first so the curve is fitted to the data rather than guessed - the same discipline BL-649's census brought to demand.

items.title: The labour read has no home, and wage competition is invisible
items.author: Claude
items.design:
FILED SO A FINDING IS NOT DELETED ALONG WITH THE SURFACE THAT DISPLAYED IT WRONGLY. BL-676 retires the Economy panel on Ben's 2026-08-29 call. Two of its three views were duplicates and one was a visibility breach, but the Workforce view was answering a real question badly rather than answering a redundant one - and after the deletion nothing answers it at all.

WHAT THE CAPTURE PASS MEASURED. The workforce table drew eighteen rows and every single one read "82% (labour short)". The panel's own doc had warned the mock fixture was uniform at 85% and said explicitly: verify against the live sim, not the CSV. Verified against the live sim - it is uniform there too.

AND IT IS NOT A BUG. `report.workforce_contention` is the POOL-LEVEL min(1, supply/demand) keyed (corp, body), and every corp in the fixture holds on one body, so one pool yields one number correctly repeated eighteen times. The view is not broken; it is showing a quantity that cannot vary in the situation it is shown in.

THE ACTUAL FINDING: BL-614 (wage competition) SUPERSEDED that scalar and nothing surfaces what replaced it. economy_system.cpp says so in terms - when a pool is contended the uniform proportional scalar no longer applies; scarce labour allocates building by building, offered wage descending (base_wage x (1 + wage_bid)), building id ascending on a tie, each granted up to its demand until the pool is spent. The marginal building takes a partial grant and those below it get nothing. The factor a building actually runs at is `report.building_labour[id]`, and the pool aggregate survives only as a reporting figure.

So there is a real mechanic here - bidding for scarce labour, and losing a building's shift to a rival who bid higher - and the only surface that ever mentioned labour rendered it as one number eighteen times. `building_labour[id]` is per building and varies; it is the quantity a player would act on.

DESIGN-OWED, AND DELIBERATELY NOT SCOPED HERE. Where this lives is open and is Ben's: a section on the building Selection card (per-building, where the number's grain actually is), a view on the Corporation dashboard beside the existing Workforce roll-up card, or a surface of its own. What is settled is only that it has no home today and that the Budget ledger's Wages tier currently has no visible consequence anywhere.

items.title: A top-bar tracker for the quantities that gate progression - level and rate, e.g. "200 Steel (+25/qtr)"
items.author: Ben
items.design:
Ben, 2026-08-30: "a tracker for important items on the top-nav bar. We should show a stockpile for steel, a new type or resource (boost), which is untradeable, and research points. These can all have an absolute value for how much is in stockpile, and an addition to the right. E.g. '200 Steel (+25/qtr)'."

THE READ IT ADDS. The header today answers "how is my money" - BALANCE, STOCKPILE (one aggregated credit figure), NET/qtr and RUNWAY. It answers nothing about the GOODS a player is accumulating, so the three quantities that gate progression are invisible unless a ledger is opened. The tracker is the always-on half of that: a level and its rate, in the shape the header already uses for money.

THE FORMAT IS BEN'S AND IS THE WHOLE SPEC: `200 Steel (+25/qtr)` - absolute stockpile, name, and the per-quarter delta to its right. The delta is the same quantity the header's NET already reports for credits, so the two read as one family rather than two conventions.

TWO OF THE THREE QUANTITIES DO NOT EXIST, and that is the item's real shape - it is a design item before it is a UI one. Do not start with the header.
  1. STEEL exists. It is an Industrial-tier resource with a live recipe chain, so its stockpile and its per-quarter movement are both readable today. This third is buildable now and is the one that proves the format.
  2. BOOST DOES NOT EXIST, and neither does untradeability. `RESOURCES.md` owns the roster and has no such resource; more importantly the model has no UNTRADEABLE PROPERTY - the nearest thing is a market opening at all-zero base_price, which is an accident of a fixture rather than a declared rule (`market_clearing.hpp`). An untradeable good is a genuinely new kind of thing: it cannot be bought, so the only way to have it is to make it, which makes it a different lever from every resource now in the game. That needs Ben's design, not an implementer's guess - what produces Boost, what consumes it, and what untradeable means at the order book (refused listing? absent from the goods table? present at no price?).
  3. RESEARCH POINTS DO NOT EXIST either - grep finds no research_point quantity anywhere in `src/world`. `RESEARCH.md` is a stub and BL-619 (RESEARCH_SYSTEM) is an open DESIGN SESSION WITH BEN, not a build slice. This third is gated on that item and must not be faked with a placeholder number.

SO THE ITEM SPLITS THREE WAYS, and only the first can start: build the tracker with Steel and a shape that takes N entries; add Boost when its design lands; add research points when BL-619 does. A header that shows one tracker is honest; one that shows three where two are zeros is not.

WHERE IT LIVES. `docs/ui/HEADER.md` owns the top bar and is the authority for the surface. `docs/economy/RESOURCES.md` owns Boost and the untradeable property. `docs/economy/RESEARCH.md` and BL-619 own research points. The header is fixed chrome on every frame, so its cost is paid always - `LAYOUT.md`'s constraint, and the reason the entry count is a design question rather than a free parameter.

CARRIED OUT OF A RETIRED SPRINT. This was the shell-chrome batch's subject (old sprint 25), which Ben deleted on 2026-08-30 as not needing a revisit. This is the one piece he kept, so it rides in sprint 25 (canvases) despite being header-grain.

items.title: Four verification instruments pass without seeing their subject, and one hangs the suite
items.author: Claude (review-queue drain, Ben's instruction)
items.design:
A green check that cannot see its subject is worse than a red one, and five are on record. Grouped because the fix is one discipline - a check must prove it LOOKED - not five unrelated repairs.

* NR-614 / NR-663 - `expect_no_clipping`'s scope is draw-list text only, so it reported '0 failure(s), 0 record(s)' over a whole 31-capture shell pass while the Corporation dashboard visibly truncated 'Workforce 76% of labour demand n' mid-word and a genuinely clipped button was on screen. ZERO RECORDS is the tell: the ledger saw nothing, so the pass is vacuous. Any check that can report zero observations must FAIL on zero, not pass.
* NR-714 - `budget_ledger_ranked.lua` is named for the Balance ledger's top-buildings ranking and captures two frames, neither of which contains it (one scrolled past it, one with the ledger shut).
* NR-606 / NR-623 - four verify scripts fail for pre-sprint reasons and `lens_strip`'s three goldens are stale by world drift (blessed 2026-06-17). The strip is the subject; the map behind it is not - re-point them at something world-independent or retire them to capture-only.
* NR-695 - `overflow_tile_v2` hung the suite: the History ledger's TILES view is a row per tile on the body, so the sweep burned CPU, collapsed memory and starved nine scripts behind it. A per-script wall clock would have turned a suite-wide stall into one red row.

items.title: Sweep 2 - base prices and the band, with the ceiling re-derived per cell
items.design:
base_price scalar {0.5, 1.0, 2.0} (whole world_gen.kepler_market.base_price table) x price band {0.25/4, 0.25/10, 0.1/20}. The two levers are COUPLED, not independent: ceil_mult is derived (> 1 + max haulage / cheapest base), so every cell re-runs haulage_measure and the manifest records whether the cell's band still clears the derivation - a violating cell is measuring an unservable tail and says so rather than reporting it as tuning.

WATCH: edge-pegged-good count per cell (ceiled-everywhere = absent industry, floored-everywhere = glut - the canon vocabulary, NR-676; today's baseline is exactly one, clean_water); GDP and net-income trends; convoy dispatches vs the 1055/802 haulage baseline (goldens cannot see trade collapse); rival sell-order floors, which ride base_price through trade_floor_multiple.

SCOPE GUARD: the law-clamp veto (2026-07-11, a law is a modifier over the market) is honoured - this sweeps the band and the reservation prices, the legitimate min/max forms; no cell may implement a price control as law.

items.author: Claude (BL-744 stage 2 field re-measure)
items.title: A processor never buys inputs worth more than its output - the anchor carried to live prices
items.design:
THE FINDING (BL-744 stage 2, 2026-09-02). With every recipe clearing the margin anchor at base price, the industrial field still collapses by tick 25 of an unwarmed lapse: expenditure runs 1.5-2.5x income from tick 4, corps go into debt, exit twelve quarters later, and the survivors are idled by their own agency. The anchor is evaluated at BASE; the sim runs at the CEILING - processed goods are ceiled in every market (10x base), so a processor pays up to 10x for inputs its recipe values at 2x, loses on every batch, and is idled as 'persistently loss-making'. Idling it removes supply, which keeps the ceiling on, which idles the next one. The ancient band takes the same wave and recovers because its chains are shallow; the industrial mid-chain (silicon, refined_copper, electronics) does not.

THE DESIGN, in the anchor's own terms: a processor's input purchase (pool bid, BL-654; auto-demand) is capped so that Σ inputs at the bid price <= output value at the current price minus the wage per batch - the M1 identity carried from authoring time to the live tick. Above the cap it does not buy and runs at the supply scalar it has (the shortfall rule: scale down, never idle - PRODUCTION.md). This is a per-recipe reservation ceiling in place of the flat reservation_mult (9x base) for processing inputs; the flat one stays for upkeep goods. It must be pure and deterministic, one rule at the one shared seam, and the rival scorer's dial_recipe reads the same number.

MEASURE FIRST: campaign_lapse --epoch 1960 --warm 0 --ticks 40 (tags diag-ind, diag-anc are the 2026-09-02 traces) with the expenditure/income split per tick; the done-when is the sprint's - operating-positive survivors that keep producing. Also owed: the agency's 'persistently loss-making' idle rule should read operating net at the recipe's own bid cap, not realised loss at the ceiling, or it will keep idling the buildings the cap is meant to save.

MEASURED 2026-09-02 (campaign_lapse debt instrumentation, industrial band, unwarmed, seeds 0/1 - build_gen/verify/lapse/debt-ind-s*/debt.csv): 129 of 129 debt entries are dominated by the EXPENDITURE flow, and in every one of them expenditure exceeded income over the four ticks before entry. But two differential runs re-order the levers. (1) Construction materials at market price are the FIRST wave: with resource_costs zeroed the early wave nearly vanishes (debtors at tick 20: 26 -> 4; median entry tick 22 -> 34), because a processor costs 25 steel at 8-10x base = 3-4k against a mine earning ~50/tick and the scorer builds through the boom. (2) The pool bids are NOT the drain: reservation_mult 0 changes nothing. (3) The tick-20 cliff is BL-746's, not this item's: with the industrial goods-upkeep draws zeroed there is no collapse at all. This item therefore drops to B and re-scopes to the two real purchase leaks - construction materials bought at the ceiling (the scorer's build tempo should price materials at the live market, and the cap here should bound them by the building's expected value) and processing inputs bought above the recipe's output value - AFTER BL-746 lands, measured on the same instrument.
--- SCOPED (Ben, 2026-09-06, on the market-work form): BOTH LEAKS, ONE ITEM ---

The two purchase leaks the 2026-09-02 differential runs separated are taken TOGETHER here, not split
and not sequenced: (1) construction materials bought at the ceiling - the scorer build tempo prices
materials at the live market, and the cap bounds them by the building expected value; (2) processing
inputs bought above the recipe output value - the M1 identity carried from authoring time to the live
tick. They share one seam and one instrument, and splitting them would have measured each against a
field the other was still distorting.

THE IDLE RULE IS NOT IN THIS ITEM. The agency "persistently loss-making" test reading operating net
at the recipe own bid cap rather than realised loss at the ceiling is BL-782 (idle rule reads the bid
cap), on Ben call - a change to the agency judgement, not to the purchase, and it wants its own
before/after.

ORDER: after BL-746 stage 2. The tick-20 cliff was BL-746 own, so a bid cap measured on today field
would be measured against a collapse it does not cause.

items.author: Claude (campaign_lapse debt instrumentation, Ben's instruction to track every balance)
items.title: The industrial band goes dark at tick 20 - an unmet goods-upkeep draw decays every building to zero
items.design:
THE FINDING (2026-09-02, campaign_lapse --epoch 1960 --warm 0, seed 0). Between tick 20 and tick 21 active buildings fall 219 -> 40 and idle rise 18 -> 198 in ONE tick, with unstaffed 0, exhausted 0 and labour unchanged (118.5 -> 119.0). 77 of 95 corps go from active to zero-active that tick, almost all extraction corps, many with positive balances. The per-corp mean supply factor decays from 1.0 at tick 1 toward 0 and reaches it at tick 20: supply_decay_permille = 50 is 5% per tick of a 0..1000 factor, so a building whose goods-upkeep draw is never met hits zero output exactly 20 ticks after it starts. In the industrial band every extraction site draws power 0.25 + timber 0.05 + stone 0.05 per tick and every processor power 0.40 + timber 0.08 + stone 0.08 (BL-708, BL-738 stage 2); power is a GRID good that reaches only network-connected tiles, generation is 18 falling to 3 units against a demand of 64, and a generator short of power throttles itself. The ancient band has no such draw and takes the same debt wave without a cliff. DIFFERENTIAL PROOF: with the two industrial goods baskets zeroed the field holds 207-257 active buildings through tick 60, income runs ahead of inputs from tick 25, produced value 16-31k/tick, debtors 19 -> 5. Nothing else was changed.

WHY IT IS A DESIGN DEFECT AND NOT A TUNING ONE. PRODUCTION.md § A shortfall scales output; it never idles says the lights go dim, not out - but a factor that decays without floor DOES go out, and it goes out for every building the grid cannot reach, which is most of them. Three levers, and Ben's call which (NR-782): (a) a FLOOR on the supply factor (e.g. 0.5) so an unmet draw halves output and never zeroes it - the rule as the doc states it; (b) NO DRAW WHERE THERE IS NO WIRE - a building the network does not reach does not draw power and does not decay for want of it (it pays the no-grid penalty some other way, or none); (c) generation bootstrap - generators exempt from the power draw, and the draw switched on per building only once its market has ever priced power. (a) and (b) are one-line rules at the one shared seam; (c) is the census's own reading of BL-708. Then re-run the debt instrument: the done-when is no one-tick cliff and a field whose active count tracks its holdings.

MEASURE with: campaign_lapse --epoch 1960 --seed N --warm 0 --ticks 60 --tag <tag>; corps.csv carries supply_factor_mean and bldg_supply_zero per corp per tick; world.csv buildings_active/idle. The 2026-09-02 traces are debt-ind-s0/s1 (the cliff) and exp-noupkeep (without it).

STAGE 1 LANDED 2026-09-02 (Ben approved NR-782 (a) and (b)). The floor: supply_floor_permille = 500 in economy.building_upkeep, parsed and range-checked like its siblings; run_building_upkeep decays to max(floor, factor - decay) and lifts a stranded factor to the floor. No wire, no draw: an unreached building's grid goods are struck from its basket before the shared draw (its ordinary goods still draw and bind), and an emptied basket draws nothing and counts as met. building_upkeep R8 (floor 500 holds at 500 over 41 ticks, recovers by the authored step, the number is the authored one, a factor below it is lifted) and R9 (an unreached building does not weaken for power on the grid; the same good off the grid decays 5 x 50; timber still binds on the unreached tile) - every row with its differential. RE-MEASURED (campaign_lapse --epoch 1960 --warm 0 --ticks 60, tags fix-ind-s0/s1): no building at factor 0 at any tick; active buildings 224 at tick 20 and 221 at tick 60 (seed 0; was 219 -> 2), 178 and 137 (seed 1); income at tick 60 13.4k / 6.8k (was 132 / 2.9k); produced value 16.1k / 10.1k (was 262 / 2.0k); debtors 11 of 86 / 6 of 73 (was 22 of 66 / 13 of 58). The ancient band is byte-identical (19 entries, same table) - it has no draw to floor. Debt entries fall 67 -> 57 and 62 -> 58 and their shape changes: starved 32 -> 7, loss-converting 30 -> 42 - the residue is BL-745's.

STAGE 2 (open, NR-782 (c) held): the field's mean supply factor settles at ~0.57 - most buildings sit AT the floor because power still does not arrive (generation 18 -> 3 units against a demand of 64; a generator short of power throttles itself; only network-reached tiles can receive it). The generation bootstrap - generators exempt from the power draw, a building drawing power only once its catchment market has priced it - is the next lever, measured on the same instrument: the done-when is the mean supply factor climbing off the floor.
--- STAGE 2 RULED (Ben, 2026-09-06, on the market-work form): NO PRICE, NO DRAW ---

NR-782 (c) is taken in its second form ONLY: A BUILDING DRAWS A GRID GOOD ONLY ONCE ITS CATCHMENT
MARKET HAS PRICED IT. Not the generator exemption, and not a scorer nudge to make generation get
built - the gate alone. Written into PRODUCTION.md § A shortfall scales output as the third rung,
beside the floor and the no-wire rule that stage 1 landed.

WHAT "PRICED IT" MEANS needs a definition before anyone builds it: the market this building clears
against (market_for_tile) has resolved a real price for the good, rather than carrying the untouched
authored default. A market that has never had supply or demand for power has never run resolve_price
on it, and that is the state the gate keys on. The predicate must be a pure function of market state
and positive-going only (once priced, always priced), or it becomes a building that flickers in and
out of its own upkeep.

THE DONE-WHEN IS A PAIR, NOT A NUMBER, and this is the whole guard: mean supply factor climbing off
0.57 toward 1, AND the power price real and moving in the markets that carry it. A supply factor that
climbs while power stays unpriced everywhere is the gate SILENCING the draw rather than letting the
industry form - and it is indistinguishable from success on the supply factor alone. Report both
columns or the measurement does not mean what it says.

STILL OPEN, deliberately: what makes generation get BUILT. Ben did not take that lever. If the gate
opens and generation still does not arrive, that is a finding for its own item, not a licence to add
a scorer weight here.

items.title: The agency idles on realised loss at the ceiling, so it idles the very buildings the bid cap exists to save
items.design:
SPLIT OUT OF BL-745 ON BEN CALL (2026-09-06, market-work form): "its own item". It is a change to the
AGENCY JUDGEMENT, not to a purchase, and it wants its own before/after rather than riding the bid cap.

THE DEFECT. The background-agency rule that idles a "persistently loss-making" building reads REALISED
loss - what the building actually paid at the live market price. Under BL-745 a processor is capped so
it does not buy inputs above its output value, and instead runs at the supply scalar it has (the
shortfall rule: scale down, never idle). But its realised operating net over the ticks BEFORE the cap
engaged is still a loss, and the rule keys on that history. So the agency goes on idling exactly the
buildings the cap was built to keep alive, and the loop BL-745 describes - idle removes supply, which
keeps the ceiling on, which idles the next one - closes again one layer up.

THE CHANGE. The test reads operating net at the RECIPE OWN BID CAP - what this building would earn
buying inputs at the price it is now willing to pay - rather than realised loss at the ceiling. A
building viable under the cap is not persistently loss-making; it is a building that was being
overcharged. One rule, at the agency seam, pure and deterministic, reading the SAME number BL-745 cap
computes - not a second copy of it, since two hand-synchronised copies is the divergence
price_band_harness exists to catch elsewhere.

SCOPE GUARD. This does NOT make the agency slower to idle in general and must not become a blanket
softening of firm exit: a building that loses money AT ITS OWN BID CAP is still loss-making and is
still idled. BL-743 (firm exit) is untouched.

MEASURE: campaign_lapse on the same instrument as BL-745, differential - the count of buildings idled
as loss-making before and after, with the survivors operating net at quarter 200. The named failure
mode is the mirror of the defect: a field that stops culling anything and fills with zombies.

DONE WHEN: the idled-as-loss-making count falls, no building viable at its bid cap is idled, and firm
exit still removes corps that cannot pay.
